steps.say: What does Postgres hosting cost on Supabase, Neon and Railway?
steps.text:
For a small Postgres database, expect about **$5/month on Railway, about $15/month on Neon and $25/month on Supabase**. All three also have a $0 free tier. None of the pages below shows a date, so check the prices on each provider's own pricing page before you commit.

| | Free | Entry paid plan | Higher tier |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Supabase** | $0 [4] | Pro: $25/month [4][6] | Team: $599/month (adds SOC 2 and SSO) [4][8]; Enterprise: custom [4] |
| **Neon** | $0 [1] | Launch: usage-based, typical spend $15/month [1] | Scale: usage-based, typical spend $701/month [1] |
| **Railway** | $0/month with $1 of monthly usage credits [2] | Hobby: $5/month including $5 of usage credits [2] | Pro: $20/month per workspace including $20 of credits [2]; Enterprise: custom [3] |

**How the usage-based prices work**
- **Supabase:** The $25 Pro plan covers your first project, and each extra project starts at $10 [6]. Above 100,000 monthly active users, you pay $0.00325 per extra user [4].
- **Neon:** You pay for compute by the hour. It costs $0.106 per CU-hour on Launch and $0.222 per CU-hour on Scale [1]. Storage on Launch is $0.35/GB-month [5]. That storage price comes from a single third-party blog, not from Neon.
- **Railway:** The plan fee comes with credits, and resource use beyond the credits is billed. RAM is $10/GB/month, CPU is $20/vCPU/month and network egress is $0.05/GB [3]. New users get a 30-day trial with a $5 one-time credit [2].

**How reliable these numbers are**
- The Neon and Railway prices come from their official pricing pages [1][2][3].
- The Supabase prices come only from third-party sites [4][6][8], because I didn't find Supabase's own pricing page. Two sources agree on each Supabase number, but confirm them at supabase.com/pricing.
- A spending-data site reports that Railway's "SMB plans" average $370 [7]. That's probably what larger teams actually spend, not a list price, so I left it out of the table.

**Which is cheapest:** Railway Hobby at $5 [2] works well if you want your app and database on one bill [6]. Neon Launch has no monthly minimum and comes to around $15 for a small database [6]. Supabase Pro has a fixed $25 fee [4] but includes more than a database: it also handles user accounts, which is where the per-user charges come from.

steps.say: We're a 20-person sales team. Compare HubSpot, Pipedrive, Salesforce, Zoho CRM and Close pricing.
steps.text:
For 20 reps, **Zoho CRM and Pipedrive are the cheapest at $280/month on their entry plans**, billed annually. **Salesforce and HubSpot cost the most** once you move up to their professional tiers, at about $1,500–$1,600/month. None of the sources is dated, and most are third-party summaries, so confirm prices on each vendor's own pricing page before you buy.

### Monthly cost for 20 users

| CRM | Plan (per user/month) | 20-user total/month |
|---|---|---|
| **Zoho CRM** | Standard $14, billed annually [11] | 20 × $14 = $280 |
| | Professional $23, billed annually [11] | 20 × $23 = $460 |
| | Enterprise $40 [4][11] | 20 × $40 = $800 |
| | Ultimate $52 [4][11] | 20 × $52 = $1,040 |
| **Pipedrive** | Lite $14 billed annually / $24 billed monthly [2] | 20 × $14 = $280 / 20 × $24 = $480 |
| | Ultimate $79 billed annually / $99 billed monthly [2] | 20 × $79 = $1,580 / 20 × $99 = $1,980 |
| **Close** | Entry plan $19, billed monthly [12] | 20 × $19 = $380 |
| | Second plan $49 [12] | 20 × $49 = $980 |
| | Third plan $109 [12] | 20 × $109 = $2,180 |
| | Top plan $149 [12] | 20 × $149 = $2,980 |
| **HubSpot** | Starter $20/seat [6][7] | 20 × $20 = $400 |
| | Professional, 20-person team [9] | $1,565/month ($18,780/yr) [9] |
| **Salesforce** | Starter/Essentials $25 [3][9][10] | 20 × $25 = $500 |
| | Professional $75 [5] or $80 [10] | 20 × $75 = $1,500 or 20 × $80 = $1,600 |
| | Enterprise $165, billed annually [10] | 20 × $165 = $3,300 |

### Things to know
- **Salesforce Professional prices don't match:** one source says $75/user [5], another says $80/user billed annually [10]. A third gives $1,600/month for 20 users [9], which works out to the $80 figure. Neither source has a date.
- **Free and solo plans won't work for 20 people.** Zoho's free plan is capped at 3 users [11], and Close's $9/month Solo plan is for one user [1].
- **Pipedrive's annual billing saves up to 42%** compared with monthly billing [2]. Its add-ons cost an extra $6.67–$41/month [8].
- **HubSpot's Professional pricing is listed per hub,** at $100–$890/month [6]. Your real cost depends on which hubs you buy, and the 20-person figure above comes from a single source [9].
- **Close:** I only found monthly-billing prices, and the source doesn't give the plan names [12]. Check close.com/pricing for annual rates.

### Only one source for these key numbers
These numbers each rest on one source, so double-check them:
- all Pipedrive prices [2]
- Close's four plan prices [12]
- Salesforce Enterprise [10]
- HubSpot Professional for 20 people [9]
- Zoho Standard and Professional [11]

Better-supported numbers: Salesforce Starter at $25 (three sources), and Zoho Enterprise and Ultimate (two sources each).

**Bottom line:** For a feature-rich mid-tier plan, Zoho Professional ($460) is the cheapest by a wide margin. Next are Close's $49 plan ($980) and Zoho Ultimate ($1,040). Salesforce Professional and HubSpot Professional both cost about $1,500–$1,600/month.

steps.text:
**Monday = Mon 9 Nov.**

You asked on Mon 9 Nov, 11:00: "We're a 20-person sales team. Compare HubSpot, Pipedrive, Salesforce, Zoho CRM and Close pricing."

Since Mon 9 Nov: **1 changed**, 6 unchanged, 5 I couldn't verify.

| What | Then (Mon 9 Nov) | Now (Thu 12 Nov) | Status |

| Zoho CRM: Standard plan price | $14 per user per month, billed annually | $14 per user per month [2] | Unchanged |
| Zoho CRM: Professional plan price | $23 per user per month, billed annually | $23 per user per month [2] | Unchanged |
| Zoho CRM: Enterprise plan price | $40 per user per month | $40 per user per month [2] | Unchanged |

| Pipedrive: Ultimate plan price | $79 per user per month, billed annually | $79 per user per month [5] | Unchanged |
| Close: Entry plan price | $19 per user per month, billed monthly | not found | Couldn't verify |
| Close: Solo plan price | $9 per month | $9 per user per month [6] | Unchanged |
| HubSpot: Starter plan price | $20 per seat per month | not found | Couldn't verify |
| HubSpot: Professional plan price for 20-person team | $1,565 per month | $2,000 per month [3] | **Changed** |
| Salesforce: Starter/Essentials plan price | $25 per user per month | not found | Couldn't verify |
| Salesforce: Professional plan price | $75 per user per month | not found | Couldn't verify |
| Salesforce: Enterprise plan price | $165 per user per month, billed annually | not found | Couldn't verify |

**No vendor pricing change since Monday is confirmed. However, Salesforce changed its editions on 3 September, before we talked, so Monday's Salesforce Enterprise figure of $165 is out of date** [1]. The only "Changed" row above (HubSpot) comes from a different source's estimate, not a confirmed price rise. Zoho and Pipedrive's entry and top plans are unchanged. Most sources are undated, so check each vendor's own pricing page before you sign.

**What's new or needs correcting**

- **Salesforce:** Enterprise and Unlimited were replaced by Core, Advanced and Max on 3 September [1]. Four sources agree on the prices, all billed annually:
  - Core: 20 × $195 [13][14] = $3,900/month
  - Advanced: 20 × $395 [15][16] = $7,900/month
  - Max: 20 × $550 [13][17] = $11,000/month
  
  The editions also include 500,000, 1,000,000 or 2.75 million Flex Credits per org per year, in that order [17]. One undated source lists "Pro Suite" at $100/user/month [7], which doesn't match Monday's $75–$80 (unverified) Professional price. That figure is single-sourced.
- **HubSpot Professional:** the new $2,000/month for 20 people is one source's estimate, worked out as "5 base + 15 × $100" [3]. It is single-sourced and undated. The same source puts year 1 at $25,500 [3], which is more than 12 × $2,000 = $24,000. The quoted text doesn't explain the gap.
- **HubSpot Starter:** sources disagree. Two say $15/seat billed annually or $20 billed monthly [23][26]. One read on 22 Oct 2026 shows $20/seat plus a promotional "starts at $7" [24]. A guide dated March 2026 says $9 [27]. For 20 seats, that's 20 × $15 [23] = $300 or 20 × $20 [26] = $400 per month.
- **HubSpot news:** Brian Halligan is back as CEO and leading an AI overhaul (article from 3 days ago). HubSpot also added AI spend caps and flexible billing [10]. The change to pay-per-result pricing for two Breeze AI agents is older, from 14 April [10].
- **Close, a correction to Monday:** the $19 I called the "entry plan" is actually the Solo plan's monthly price. Solo is $9 billed annually [18][20]. Close's full price list:

  | Plan | Annual billing | Monthly billing |
  |---|---|---|
  | Solo | $9 [19] | $19 [19] |
  | Essentials | $35 [19] | $49 [19] |
  | Growth | $99 [19] | $109 [19] |
  | Scale | $139 [19] | $149 [19] |

  For 20 users, Essentials billed annually is 20 × $35 [19] = $700/month. These sources price Solo per user and don't mention a one-user cap, so check close.com/pricing for its limits.
- **Pipedrive:** Premium dropped from $59 to $49 in July 2026 [11]. That's before Monday, but my earlier answer left it out. The Projects add-on now shows "Starting from $16", down from $16.66 [9]. That source is undated.
- **Zoho CRM:** no change. Two sources now agree on $14, $23, $40 and $52 per user per month [2][8].

steps.say: How much does Zoho Books cost in India?
warnings: I couldn't match ₹884 to a current source. Treat it as unverified.
steps.text:
**Zoho Books in India has a free plan for businesses with turnover under ₹25 lakh. Paid plans run from about ₹749 to ₹7,999 a month if you pay yearly, plus GST [3][7].** All eight sources are third-party blogs with no publication date, and they disagree on some plans. Check the final price on Zoho's official India pricing page before you buy.

| Plan | Per month, billed yearly | Per month, billed monthly |
|---|---|---|
| Free | ₹0, turnover under ₹25 lakh [3][6][8] | ₹0 [3] |
| Standard | ₹749 [1][3][4][7] | ₹899 [3][6][7] |
| Professional | ₹1,499 [3][5]. One source says ₹1,249 [1] | ₹1,799 [3][5][6] |
| Premium | ₹2,999 [3]. One source says ₹2,499 [1] | ₹3,599 [3][6] |
| Elite | ₹4,999 [1][3] | ₹5,999 [3][6] |
| Ultimate | ₹7,999 [3][5][7]. One source says ₹8,332 [1] | ₹9,599 [3][5][6]. Two sources say ₹9,999 [2][8] |

**Where the sources disagree:**
- **Standard and Elite:** The sources mostly agree.
- **Premium yearly price:** Only one source gives each figure, ₹2,999 [3] and ₹2,499 [1], so neither is confirmed.
- **Professional and Ultimate:** Most sources give the prices in the table, but one or two disagree.
- **Mixed-up billing:** Some sources seem to mix monthly and yearly prices. For example, one lists Standard at ₹899, Professional at ₹1,499 and Premium at ₹2,999 [2]. That mixes Standard's monthly price with the yearly prices of the other two.

**GST:** These prices don't include GST [4][7]. One source says to add 18% GST to every paid plan [8]. For example, Standard billed yearly works out to ₹749 [3] × 1.18 ≈ ₹884 (unverified) a month.

Prices are per organisation [6]. For the current official prices, go to zoho.com/in/books/pricing.

steps.say: Does Render have a free tier for Postgres, and what does the cheapest paid Render Postgres plan cost?
warnings: I couldn't match $9 to a current source. Treat it as unverified.
steps.text:
**Yes, Render has a free Postgres tier, but most sources say a free database expires 30 days after you create it. The cheapest paid plan is Basic-256mb at $6 a month [2][4].** All five sources are undated third-party blogs, not Render's own pages. Check render.com/pricing before you decide.

**Free tier**
- Three sources say free Render Postgres databases expire after 30 days [1][3][4]. After that you need to upgrade or move your data elsewhere [1].
- One source disagrees. It says the free tier includes a PostgreSQL database "with no time limit" [5]. It's outnumbered, so plan around the 30-day limit unless Render's own docs say otherwise.

**Cheapest paid plan**
- Basic-256mb (0.1 CPU, 256 MB RAM) costs $6 a month [2][4]. Two sources give this price. A third gives a range of about $6–7 a month [1].
- Storage is billed separately at $0.30 per GB per month, prorated by the second [2]. Only one source gives this price.
- For example, 10 GB of storage would cost 10 × $0.30 [2] = $3. With the $6 plan [2], that's about $9 (unverified) a month.

None of the sources are official or dated, so check the current prices and the free-tier rules at render.com/pricing and in Render's Postgres docs.

steps.say: Compare Linear and Basecamp pricing for our 8-person team.
steps.text:
**For 8 people, Linear's paid plans cost about $80–$144 a month and Basecamp's cost about $120–$299 a month. The sources disagree on several prices, and Basecamp's flat-fee plans have user caps they don't spell out.** All eight sources are undated third-party pages (checked 9 Nov 2026), so confirm on linear.app/pricing and basecamp.com/pricing before you buy.

| Plan | Price | Cost for 8 people per month |
|---|---|---|
| Linear Basic, billed yearly | $10 per user [7] | 8 × $10 [7] = $80 |
| Linear Basic, other figure | $12 per user [2] | 8 × $12 [2] = $96 |
| Linear Business, billed yearly | $16 per user [1][7] | 8 × $16 [1][7] = $128 |
| Linear Business, billed monthly | $18 per user [2][7] | 8 × $18 [2][7] = $144 |
| Linear Enterprise | Not published [6] | Ask Linear |
| Basecamp Plus | $15 per user [2][4] | 8 × $15 [2][4] = $120 |
| Basecamp Pro Unlimited, billed yearly | $299 flat [2][4][8]. One source says $199 [3] | $299 or $199 |
| Basecamp Pro Unlimited, billed monthly | $349 [4]. One source says $329 [3] | $349 or $329 |

**What to watch for**
- **Linear Basic:** $10 [7] and $12 [2] each come from one source. The $12 is probably the price if you pay monthly, but that isn't confirmed. Business is better supported: $16 billed yearly and $18 billed monthly [1][7].
- **Linear's older plan names:** One source lists "Standard" at $8 and "Plus" at $14 [5]. These look like outdated plans, so I've left them out.
- **Basecamp's cheaper flat plans:** One source lists Freelancer at $29, Pro at $79 and Pro Plus at $99 a month, with "user caps" [3]. If 8 people fit under those caps, Basecamp could cost less than Linear. No source says what the caps are. Only one source lists "Start" at $11 a month [5].
- **Pro Unlimited:** The sources clash. Three say $299 billed yearly [2][4][8], but another says $199 [3]. For monthly billing, $349 [4] and $329 [3] each come from a single source.
- **Free plans:** One source mentions a free Basecamp plan [8], but none give its limits. None mention a free Linear plan.

**Bottom line:** On per-user plans, Linear Basic (8 × $10 [7] = $80) is cheaper than Basecamp Plus (8 × $15 [2][4] = $120). Basecamp's flat plans could cost less, depending on their user caps. The two tools also do different jobs: Linear tracks software issues and Basecamp manages projects. The right fit may matter more than the price difference.
